uncited: Photometric loss minimizes the difference between rendered pixels and input training images during joint optimization [Parent](7799-photometric-reconstruction-loss.md).

*   **Inputs:** Predicted color $\hat{C}(r_i)$ and ground-truth color $C(r_i)$ for sample $i$ along ray $r_i$; hyperparameters $\lambda$ (D-SSIM weight), $\lambda_{\text{dist}}$, $\lambda_{\text{normal}}$.
*   D-SSIM is computed over local windows (typically $3\times3$ or $11\times11$ pixels) in the 2D image plane.
Compute the differentiable SSIM loss $\mathcal{L}_{\text{D-SSIM}}$ between the rendered and ground-truth images.
*   **Time Complexity:** Linear in the number of pixels and samples per pixel.
D-SSIM adds a constant factor related to window size.
*   **Memory Complexity:** Linear in image resolution for storing intermediate SSIM maps.
*   **When to use:** Standard for novel view synthesis when perceptual quality is prioritized.
*   **When not to use:** Real-time applications where speed is critical; scenes with significant lighting changes where photometric consistency is low.
Photometric loss is a standard component in differentiable rendering and neural radiance field (NeRF) optimization.

The weight is calculated as the L2 norm of the color difference divided by the minimum L2 norm across all samples, clamped to $[1, 10]$ [S2].

The claim states that the weight is calculated as the L2 norm of the color difference divided by the minimum L2 norm across all samples, clamped to [1, 10]. Source [S2] explicitly defines the raw weight w̃_i as the ratio of the L2 norm of the color difference (||Ĉ(r_i) - C(r_i)||_2) to the minimum L2 norm across all N samples (min_{i} ||Ĉ(r_i) - C(r_i)||_2). It further states that the final weight w_i is defined as clamp(w̃_i), where clamp(·) clips the value into [1, 10]. Thus, every part of the claim is directly supported by the text and equations in Source [S2].
